correctness.rationale: Percolation component of seed is exactly the one-generation epidemic set on a tree. At p near 0 only one open incident edge contributes to Var at first order, giving deg(v)p. At q=1-p near 0 a single closed edge e removes s_e(v) vertices, giving Var=q sum_e s_e(v)^2+O(q^2). Edge-separation double-counting proves sum_e s_e(v)^2=nD_T(v)-W(T); finite-tree uniformity in root holds. For every internal vertex a branch size b<n/2 exists and movement into that branch increases farness by n-2b; hence farness maximizers are leaves. Maximum-degree vertices are internal for n>=3. Independent exact percolation enumeration of P3 reproduces center-minus-leaf p(p-1)(p^2+3p-1). Recomputed edge identity and leaf farness maximizers for all unlabeled trees on 3..9 vertices; these finite checks corroborate the general argument.
residual_risks: Does not classify all intermediate parameter switches or all graph types; polynomial and uniform asymptotics rely on finite fixed trees.

evidence: General network epidemic-percolation frameworks include homogeneous trees as special models.
